summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of acute on chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia, coronary atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3B chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema due to fluid overload. The exacerbation was triggered by missing multiple heart failure medications, including amiodarone, spironolactone, digoxin, and metoprolol, and dietary indiscretions. He was treated with IV furosemide initially, then transitioned to oral torsemide with a one-time metolazone boost. His weight decreased from 137.4 kg to 129.2 kg, near his known dry weight. He had a transient rise in creatinine to 2.7, consistent with cardiorenal physiology, and was evaluated by nephrology who confirmed stage 3B CKD without need for dialysis. A positive urinalysis was treated briefly with ceftriaxone, but culture was negative. He remained on home medications for heart failure and arrhythmia, with spironolactone resumed after potassium normalized. He was enrolled in the PACT program for outpatient support and discharged home with close follow-up in cardiology and nephrology.
